newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NML says risk market still competitive.
newsitem.headline: NML says risk market still competitive.

text.p: The risk insurance market remains extremely competitive despite early signs of less aggressive pricing by some companies, National Mutual Life Association (NML) managing director Tony Killen said on Tuesday.
Killen said National Mutual faced growing competition in the sector -- which includes term, trauma and income protection -- but remained market leader for both individual and group products.
"We're seeing some pricing in the market that I don't think will be sustainable," Killen told reporters after a lunch address to the Australian Institute of Company Directors.
"In fact you are starting to see some competitors, having priced extremely aggresively, now starting to pull back," he added.
Killen said risk and superannuation were growing sectors of the insurance market, while the redeployment of superannuation savings as people retired was an emerging opportunity.
"We've got some good growth prospects here, but it is very competitive," he said.
National Mutual Life contributed A$111 million to the A$175.5 million net profit recorded by National Mutual Holdings Ltd in the six months to March 31.
